findings.claim: smine-permissions' candidate→rule derivation (SKILL.md:39-46, new in this diff v0.1.0) groups Bash grants into a family by "program + subcommand" and allowlists `Bash(<program> <subcommand> *)`. For a program with no real subcommand grammar (curl, wget, nc, ssh, docker exec, psql, …) the first non-flag token it treats as the "subcommand" is actually the first argument (a URL, host, or flag value), so the derived rule is `Bash(curl https *)` / `Bash(curl http *)` etc. — a wildcard-suffixed rule that matches effectively any curl invocation with that scheme, i.e. unrestricted outbound HTTP(S) from an allowlisted shell command. The skill's own invariant ("never a rule broader than what the evidence granted", Rules section) is violated by construction for this whole class of programs: nothing in the derivation step special-cases programs lacking subcommand structure. Once ≥2 distinct sessions have granted any such command (the sole and only gate, step 4: "needs ≥2 distinct sessions"), smine-permissions proposes the over-broad rule to `proposals/permissions.json`; smine-apply (SKILL.md:31, the new permissions-kind route in this diff v1.28) appends the rule string verbatim to `permissions.allow` in `settings/claude_code/settings.json` on a single `+` vote, or — in `auto-apply: always` mode with no `dimensions` argument (smine-apply SKILL.md:32: "absent = all") — with ZERO human review at all, since `permissions` is not named in the auto-apply dimension vocabulary (`context, routines, skills`) and "absent = all" does not explicitly exclude it. After the rule lands, every future `curl https ...` (or whichever scheme) call runs with no prompt, including one fetching and piping an attacker-controlled payload to a shell.
findings.fix: In smine-permissions step 2 (candidate→rule), require the derived Bash rule to keep every argument token of the observed commands literal (no wildcard) unless the program is on a known-safe subcommand allowlist (git, gh, go, make, npm, …); for any other program, the proposed rule must retain the full argument list verbatim (effectively one rule per exact command) or be rejected from auto-derivation entirely and routed `human` for manual narrowing.
findings.evidence: Re-read skills/smine/smine-permissions/SKILL.md lines 36-49 (step 1 Extract & merge, step 2 Candidate→rule) in the committed head: the family-grouping rule at line 39 is literally "Bash commands sharing a program + subcommand" with only the `gh pr view` example given; the derivation rule at line 44-46 gives no exception for subcommand-less programs. Re-read skills/smine/smine-apply/SKILL.md line 31 (permissions-kind apply route: appends the rule string verbatim to permissions.allow) and line 32 (auto-apply `always` mode dimension vocabulary `context, routines, skills`, "absent = all" — permissions not named, not excluded). Both files are new/changed in this diff (smine-permissions is version 0.1.0, brand new; smine-apply's permissions-kind branch is new in v1.28 per its changelog.json). No special-casing, no argument-literal fallback, and no explicit always-mode exclusion for the permissions kind exists anywhere in either file. The claim survives re-check: the mechanism as specified permits deriving and auto-applying an over-broad shell allowlist rule from two session grants with no required human judgment.

findings.claim: smine-batch's new Permissions capture (SKILL.md:58, v1.28 in this diff) records `{tool, command, decision}` for every prompted-and-granted tool/command verbatim — no redaction, no secret-scrubbing step is specified anywhere in this skill or its consumer. Any session where the user approved a command carrying an inline credential (`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" ...`, a `postgres://user:pass@host/db` connection string, an API key passed as a CLI flag, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=... command`, etc. — all common, everyday developer command shapes) has that full command line written verbatim into `sessions/<name>/json/<batch>.json` (smine-batch §4) — a file the skill treats as a persisted, authoritative artifact alongside the batch markdown (not gitignored, unlike e.g. `proposals/votes-archive.jsonl` which this same skill family explicitly marks gitignored). smine-permissions (SKILL.md §2, "note names the concrete granted command") then copies the same verbatim command into `proposals/permissions.json`'s evidence, a second persisted file, and that evidence is rendered to human voters. Neither file nor either skill's prose contains any secret-pattern redaction, truncation, or scrubbing instruction before the command string is written.
findings.fix: Before writing a captured `command` string to the batch JSON or to permissions-proposal evidence, redact common credential shapes (Bearer/API tokens, basic-auth userinfo in URLs, `key=value` env-var assignments matching known secret-name patterns) with a fixed placeholder, and flag the entry so a human reviewer knows redaction occurred; alternatively, drop the argument portion of any command matching a secret heuristic and keep only the program+subcommand prefix.
findings.evidence: Re-read skills/smine/smine-batch/SKILL.md line 58 in the committed head: "record per session {tool, command, decision} for each prompted-and-granted tool/command ... This is capture, not proposal-authoring" — no redaction clause anywhere in the file (grepped for redact/scrub/mask/sanitize: no hits). Re-read skills/smine/smine-permissions/SKILL.md step 2 ("note names the concrete granted command") and step 0 (output `proposals/permissions.json ... the single authoritative artifact", no gitignore note, contrasted explicitly elsewhere in the same skill family — smine-apply SKILL.md "Disposition ledger" bullet — where `votes-archive.jsonl` IS called out as "(gitignored)"). The absence of that same gitignore callout for the batch JSON and permissions.json, combined with zero redaction logic in the capture path, is a verifiable textual fact, not a speculative read. Both the batch-JSON capture and its downstream permissions-proposal copy are new in this diff (smine-batch v1.28, smine-permissions v0.1.0).

notes: Scope: chunk "skills" (48 files, markdown SKILL.md + changelog.json + a handful of skill-bundled workflows/*.js; no server/web code, no running endpoint in this chunk, so ACTION-REVIEW-SEC-003's curl-probe is not applicable anywhere in-chunk — the two findings are settled by direct re-read of the exact procedural text that will govern unattended agent behavior, which is the closest analogue to a probe available for prose-governed automation. No scope was removed from this chunk's assigned files. Cross-chunk notes: smine-permissions' allowlist-widening path (security-BLK-1) terminates in settings/claude_code/settings.json, which is outside this chunk — the station/other lanes should confirm whether that file's current permissions.allow already contains any such over-broad curl/wget/nc-style wildcard rule (would turn this from a newly-introduced risk into an already-live one). Likewise the claim that session JSON / permissions.json are NOT gitignored (security-BLK-2) rests on the absence of a counter-statement in this chunk's files plus the contrasting explicit gitignore callout for votes-archive.jsonl in smine-apply; a .gitignore file itself is outside this chunk and was not read — flagging as a cross-chunk fact to verify, not chasing it further here.
